title: Prefix-cache correctness eval to detect semantic drift from cache hits
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Problem: We have observed rare cases where prefix/KV cache hits change the model's generated output semantics (reordered tokens, omitted facts, or different function call selections). This ticket defines a reproducible evaluation and continuous monitoring pipeline that detects semantic drift introduced by cache hits across model/config changes.

Goals: 1) Build a deterministic eval harness that measures semantic divergence between cache-hit and cache-miss executions for the same request prefix. 2) Define signal thresholds and automated alerts that integrate with CI and canary rollouts. 3) Provide triage artifacts (diffs, per-token attribution, embeddings similarity) to quickly identify if divergence is harmful.

Scope and constraints: - Focus on prefix/KV cache correctness (not broader batching or scheduler differences). - Evaluate across representative model families we serve (small/med/large quantized variants) and relevant configs (kv_sharding, kv_cache_ttl, cache_key_normalization). - Must run within CI time budgets; include a smaller fast suite for pre-merge checks and a larger nightly job. - Avoid false positives from nondeterministic sampling: use deterministic decoding or fixed seeds for stochastic models in eval, and track temperature/stochasticity separately.

Deliverables: - A dataset of ~300 curated prompts grouped into families likely to be cache-sensitive (dialogue continuations, long-context references, structured outputs, tool-calling prompts). - Test harness that: a) runs each prompt with cache disabled (cold) and with cache replay (warm) and b) captures token-level traces, function-calling events, and final structured outputs. - Metrics computed per prompt: token edit distance, normalized embedding cosine, function-call parity, structured field diffs, and a summary risk score. - Integration into our CI: PR gate that runs the fast suite and posts results to the PR check with delta summary; nightly job running the full suite and feeding the console regression dashboard. - Runbook describing triage steps and recommended mitigations (cache key normalization fixes, per-model cache invariants, fallback to cold decoding).
acceptance_criteria: Fast suite (50 prompts) runs in <10 minutes in CI and fails PR checks when risk score > 0.15
Nightly full suite generates historical baseline and posts metrics to console/regressions dashboard
Automated artifact links (token diffs, emb histograms, function-call mismatches) available for every flagged prompt
Canary rollout gating: a regression in the nightly suite must block model/config promoting to stable until triaged
Documented runbook and ownership for investigations with example mitigation PRs
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Avery. Observed customer report about assistant returning different JSON fields when prefix cache active. Initial proposal drafted.

2026-02-24 - Spike completed: ran 100 random prompts across two models and reproduced several deterministic token reordering cases when warm KV cache used. Spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/prefix-cache-spike (internal doc)

2026-02-26 - Design review with Priya Nair and Liam O'Connor. Agreed on metric set: token edit distance, embedding cosine (sentence-transformer), and function-call parity. Priya requested including structured-output-aware diffs for JSON outputs.

2026-03-01 - Initial harness prototype (bench/kv-cache-eval) submitted as draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1458. Includes deterministic runner and an artifacts collector. @Diego started wiring CI job.

2026-03-04 - Review feedback from runtime team: need to include tests for kv_sharding boundary conditions and ensure the harness supports multi-GPU prefix reconstruction. Added ENG-8120 as dependency.

2026-03-07 - Canary gating proposal posted to console-team: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Prefix+Cache+Regression+Gating. Console team suggested adding a visual diff widget; added as follow-up (ENG-8502).

2026-03-08 - Running expanded sample set (300 prompts) locally. Found a reproducible case where cached KV with quantized model 7B-q8 causes different tool selection. Drafting mitigations: strict cache key normalization and a 'prefer-cold-on-toolcall' flag.
